title: Dilated proximal bowel with a hernia on CT: incarcerated inguinal hernia causing small bowel obstruction
vignette: A 64-year-old woman comes to the emergency department due to a 2-day history of worsening abdominal pain. She has a history of gallstones but has had no surgery due to high operative risk. Medical history includes chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, hypertension, and remote cervical cancer treated with surgery and chemotherapy. Abdominal CT scan shows multiple dilated small bowel loops with a decompressed distal ileum, and an abnormal bowel indicated by the arrow: the arrow points to a small bowel loop extending outside the peritoneal cavity into the left inguinal area. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's current condition?

clues.text: multiple dilated small bowel loops with a decompressed distal ileum
clues.note: Dilated bowel PROXIMAL to and decompressed bowel DISTAL to a point = a mechanical small bowel obstruction with a transition point.

clues.text: small bowel loop extending outside the peritoneal cavity into the left inguinal area
clues.note: A bowel loop herniating OUTSIDE the peritoneal cavity into the inguinal region that is trapped = an INCARCERATED inguinal hernia (the transition point/cause of obstruction).

whatMatters: CT shows a mechanical small bowel OBSTRUCTION (dilated proximal loops, decompressed distal ileum) with a bowel loop herniating OUTSIDE the peritoneal cavity into the inguinal area = an INCARCERATED (trapped) inguinal hernia as the cause; incarceration risks strangulation. Answer B.
strategy: Read the CT: SBO with a transition point where bowel exits the peritoneal cavity into the groin = incarcerated inguinal hernia. Reject the history-based distractors: gallstone ileus (gallstone impacted at ileocecal valve + pneumobilia, no hernia), malrotation (infancy; left-sided large bowel/right small bowel), volvulus (mesenteric 'whirl sign' transition), and peritoneal adhesions (INTRAperitoneal transition point, common post-surgery - but here the loop is EXTRAperitoneal in a hernia).

eliminations.label: Gallstone ileus - impacted stone + pneumobilia
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a large gallstone eroding into the gut and impacting (often at the ileocecal valve), causing SBO. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: CT would show an obstructing stone and often pneumobilia, not a bowel loop herniating into the groin. ✅ Correct if: obstructing gallstone + air in the biliary tree (Rigler triad).

eliminations.label: Intestinal malrotation - infancy
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: incomplete in-utero midgut rotation with abnormal peritoneal (Ladd) bands. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it presents mainly in infancy and shows left-sided large bowel/right-sided small bowel, not an inguinal hernia in an adult. ✅ Correct if: neonatal bilious emesis with malposition.

eliminations.label: Intestinal volvulus - whirl sign
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a bowel loop twisting around its mesentery. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: CT classically shows a mesenteric 'whirl sign' at the transition, not bowel herniating outside the peritoneal cavity. ✅ Correct if: sigmoid/cecal volvulus with whirl sign.

eliminations.label: Peritoneal adhesion - intraperitoneal transition
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: fibrous bands (often post-surgical) trapping bowel and causing SBO - the most common overall cause. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: adhesions give an INTRAperitoneal transition point, whereas here the loop exits the peritoneal cavity into a hernia (extraperitoneal). ✅ Correct if: SBO with an intraperitoneal transition and prior abdominal surgery.

reasoning: CT shows dilated proximal small bowel and decompressed distal ileum = mechanical small bowel obstruction
The transition point is a bowel loop herniating outside the peritoneal cavity into the inguinal area
A trapped inguinal hernia = incarceration (risk of strangulation)
mechanism: SMALL BOWEL OBSTRUCTION (SBO) is a mechanical (or functional) blockage of intraluminal flow. Mechanical SBO produces DILATION of bowel PROXIMAL to the obstruction and DECOMPRESSION DISTAL to it, with pain, nausea, bilious vomiting, and distension; CT is the test of choice to find the specific site (transition point), assess severity (partial vs complete), and detect complications (ischemia, perforation). Common mechanical causes are ADHESIONS (most common overall, usually postoperative), HERNIAS, and tumors. Here the CT shows a small bowel loop extending OUTSIDE the peritoneal cavity into the inguinal region - an INGUINAL HERNIA that has become INCARCERATED (trapped and non-reducible), acting as the transition point and cause of SBO. Incarceration raises the risk of STRANGULATION (compromised blood supply -> ischemia/necrosis) and warrants urgent surgical evaluation. The distractors have distinct imaging: gallstone ileus (obstructing stone + pneumobilia), malrotation (pediatric malposition), volvulus (mesenteric whirl sign), and adhesions (intraperitoneal transition without a hernia).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Surgery/GI > small bowel obstruction: dilated proximal + decompressed distal bowel; causes = adhesions (#1), hernias, tumors; incarcerated hernia = trapped loop -> strangulation risk; CT identifies transition point.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: SBO with a bowel loop herniating out of the peritoneal cavity into the groin = incarcerated inguinal hernia.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on small bowel obstruction, transition point, incarcerated vs strangulated hernia, or pneumobilia? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Gallstone ileus = stone + pneumobilia; malrotation = infancy; volvulus = whirl sign; adhesion = intraperitoneal transition.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: Abdominal CT (stem): dilated proximal small bowel + decompressed distal ileum with a loop herniating OUTSIDE the peritoneum into the groin = incarcerated inguinal hernia.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: SBO transition at an out-of-peritoneum groin loop = incarcerated inguinal hernia (strangulation risk).

keywords.front: SBO with a groin hernia transition point

keywords.back: Dilated proximal + decompressed distal bowel (transition point)

keywords.front: Most common cause of SBO overall

firstAid.detail: Surgery: hernia loop outside peritoneum = SBO transition; strangulation risk.
GI > adhesions, gallstone ileus, volvulus, malrotation.

memoryHook: Bowel ballooned upstream, empty downstream, and one loop squeezing out into the groin - a hernia caught the gut (incarcerated); free it before it strangles.
